subject: US3122047
CRF_evidence: The unblinding form names mRNA-1273 as dose 2. The Day 29 exposure audit says treatment was not given.
cross_check: ADSL DOSE2FL=N; no second blinded administration in EX. One of 50, not an extra case.
record_to_request: IRT, vaccination and accountability records; completion instructions.

subject: US3812197
CRF_evidence: The unblinding form names placebo as dose 2; the Day 29 exposure audit says No.
cross_check: ADSL DOSE2FL=N; only a first blinded placebo dose in EX.

subject: US3172360
CRF_evidence: Unblinding form says first dose was not administered. The visit form says it was given, and a monitor cites the treatment system to challenge the entry.
cross_check: Blinded EX shows mRNA-1273 on 27 August 2020; ADSL DOSE1FL=Y.
record_to_request: IRT transaction, pharmacy dispensing and query closure.

subject: US3142043
CRF_evidence: Between January and April 2021 assignment changed from vaccine to placebo, back to vaccine, then to placebo after a query citing IRT.
cross_check: Final assignment agrees with ADSL; both blinded EX administrations are placebo.
record_to_request: Distinguish the audit history from the final assignment.

subject: US3932018
CRF_evidence: The AE narrative acknowledges joint aches from 28 August to 23 September 2020 and says an illness visit was inadvertently missed. A deviation was to be reported.
cross_check: AE-005 retained in S3/S27. PCR: routine samples on 28 August and 24 September, no illness-labelled sample during the episode. Five S3 DV/ADDV rows and their supplementary explanations do not explicitly identify this missed visit.
record_to_request: Original call and diary timestamps, deviation ID, reason and site follow-up.

subject: US3572076
CRF_evidence: The September 1 contact date was first entered on 9 April 2021, a 220-day gap.
cross_check: Two negative illness-visit MB records carry 1 September 2020. This is a late field entry, not evidence of a delayed swab.
record_to_request: Contemporaneous contact log and form-creation timestamp.

subject: US3812197
CRF_evidence: Safety queried a fax described as serious versus an electronic entry of non-serious. The site explained a severity grade change. The seriousness field went No → Yes → No.
cross_check: Symptomatic COVID, AE-001, is non-serious in S3 and S27. The available query does not by itself settle clinical seriousness.
record_to_request: Original safety fax, seriousness criterion and signed reconciliation.

subject: US3212013
CRF_evidence: Safety questioned whether bleeding preceded vaccination and whether medical history should be amended.
cross_check: Two abnormal uterine bleeding records, 27 August and 22 September 2020, are retained as serious in S3 and S27.
record_to_request: Source records if assessing whether these describe distinct episodes or causality.

subject: US3722066
CRF_evidence: A site response describes combining a record with a serious event; the audit trail discusses separating the original illness and its worsening.
cross_check: S3/S27 retain initial positive COVID as non-serious, worsening COVID as serious and COVID pneumonia as serious.
record_to_request: Use linked episode IDs before counting diagnoses as separate clinical illnesses.

subject: US3742253
CRF_evidence: The field was corrected to positive and the site distinguished the 25 September collection from the 3 October result date.
cross_check: The September 25 MB results are positive; September 27 has a negative result on a different date.
record_to_request: Specimen accession numbers before interpreting a change as reversal of a laboratory result.

subject: US3222189
CRF_evidence: In response to a safety query, the site said it learned of the admission too late after discharge to obtain a hospital swab.
cross_check: No dated qualifying PCR identified in the released lab data around the October 2–3 encephalopathy admission. This does not make the illness COVID.
record_to_request: Hospital virology/clinical records and site notification log.

subject: US3932147
CRF_evidence: A monitor identified cough, shortness of breath and five other complaints on 20–27 September 2020, beyond the first post-dose week. The site confirmed it did not complete the illness visit.
cross_check: The seven complaints are separate AE records in S5, S3 and S27. Production MB has no dated PCR during this episode. Two S3 deviations for late COVID assessment are dated 16 September, before reported symptom onset; neither can be assigned to this illness by its date alone.
record_to_request: Dated site contact, illness assessment and deviation ID.

subject: US3632127
CRF_evidence: The medical monitor asked whether intermittent cough was assessed for possible COVID. The site replied that there was no illness visit and that it had documented a deviation.
cross_check: AE-004: 3–13 January 2021. No PCR in the production ledger during the cough; a routine sample is dated 15 January. The sole S3 DV row describes a December visit, without expressly identifying this illness.
record_to_request: Site deviation report and contact date.

finding: Local test without a site illness visit
subject: US3242397
CRF_evidence: The site explained that the illness visit had not been done and that the test was performed at an outside hospital clinic.
cross_check: A positive laboratory result is recorded on 1 November 2020, despite no site illness visit for that initial test.
record_to_request: Independent evidence on why an absent site visit need not mean an absent test.

subject: US3162078
CRF_evidence: A monitor identified 14 August 2020 as onset in source; the site renumbered an existing entry from day 1 to day 6 and was asked to mark intervening unassessed days accordingly.
cross_check: An illness-labelled positive PCR is recorded on 19 August. The submitted symptomatic COVID AE starts on 14 August. This is a retrospective correction, not evidence of fictitious testing.
record_to_request: Original dated symptom and contact diary.

subject: US3952033
CRF_evidence: Two EUA forms describe serious pericarditis over identical dates, 31 October–3 November 2020. The monitor explicitly flagged AE-005 as overlapping AE-004 and requested reconciliation.
cross_check: BLA S10 p.295 (Bates 3789887) and S3/S27 retain AE-004 as serious with the same dates. Strong evidence of duplicate cleanup; the pericarditis is not missing.
record_to_request: Query closure and safety case identifier for formal row disposition.

subject: US3252166
CRF_evidence: Safety and coding queried reporting thyroidectomy as the AE and requested the underlying diagnosis and documentation of the operation as a procedure.
cross_check: In production, thyroid cancer is a serious AE and surgery appears in the narratives. The record changed representation; the operation did not disappear from the participant history.
record_to_request: Link the procedure record and the underlying clinical event before counting missing illnesses.

subject: US3252166
CRF_evidence: The BLA form names metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma. The AE narrative and procedure queries explicitly discuss thyroidectomy.
cross_check: See the corresponding EUA record and query. This provides clinical context, not a one-to-one match of AE identifiers or dates.
record_to_request: Procedure date, oncology report, and AE-to-procedure cross-reference.

subject: US3172069
CRF_evidence: The EUA form records prostate cancer. The EUA seriousness field is Yes.
cross_check: The licensing demographics contain the participant, but S3 and S27 have no AE rows for this participant, and no substantive licensing CRF for this ID was found in the indexed public files.
record_to_request: Licensing CRF, case disposition and safety reconciliation for this specific participant.
